Drag across the plot to reshape the curve; the network's curve follows. ONE NETWORK, TWO MACHINES, the same kernels //! on both - the GPU learning kit's (`src/gpu/zn_mlp.zig`): //! //! * THE CPU trains IN A JOB - a Web Worker in a browser, a thread of the program's own natively - as a chain: one //! job in flight, each a few steps of the kernels on their CPU twin, the training's state shipped back to the page //! and out again with the next job, with the drawing as it is then (`kernels.trainSteps`). One box runs the very //! same job on the frame's own thread instead, to see what the worker saves. //! * THE GPU trains IN BATCHES: many steps recorded as one submission, then the curve and the loss asked back, the //! frame never waiting for them (`submitBatch`, `collectBatch`). //! //! The toggle hands the training from one machine to the other - the weights, both moments, the step count - once the //! work in flight has landed (`switchMachines`). The panel chooses the network and how it learns. What to look for: //! //! * the network's curve bending toward each new stroke while the stroke is still being drawn; //! * the dot orbiting smoothly, the frames near 16.7 ms: the training is ELSEWHERE - and, with the box ticked, the //! dot stuttering, the same work now ON the frame; //! * the steps a second at a flip: the CPU is slow, the GPU is not, and the loss carries on across it. const std = @import("std"); const Io = std.Io; const z = @import("zimr"); const zm = @import("zm"); /// Frames slower than this on average are late: a 60 Hz frame is 16.7 ms. const late_frame_ms: f32 = 20.0; /// A batch on the GPU that takes longer than this to come back has its steps halved: four frames. const longest_batch_seconds: f32 = 4.0 / 60.0; the plot is drawn on, not panned - and its series in the plot's f64. plot_state: plot_ui.PlotState, sample_xs: [sketch.sample_count]f64, drawing_ys: [sketch.sample_count]f64, network_ys: [sketch.sample_count]f64, /// Where the pointer was on the frame before, while a stroke lasts, in the plot's units. stroke_last: Vec2, /// THE LOSS CHART: when the page started (`wgpu.nowMs`), and a point per landing - its seconds since then and its /// loss - of every `loss_stride`-th landing (`recordLoss`). started_at_ms: f64, loss_seconds: [loss_room]f64, loss_values: [loss_room]f64, loss_count: usize, loss_stride: u32, landings_since_loss_point: u32, loss_plot_state: plot_ui.PlotState, /// THE MACHINES: the one training now, and the toggle's choice - taken once the work in flight has landed /// (`switchMachines`). machine: Machine, wanted_machine: Machine, /// THE GPU: the kit's kernels on the device - their pipelines made in the background - and the network on it, /// made when the GPU first trains and again at each fresh start. No pipe where the device would not make one. gpu_pipe: ?Pipe, gpu_network: ?*Network, /// The batch on the GPU: whether one is in flight, its two readbacks - the curve and the loss - and the steps a /// batch takes (`steerStepsPerBatch`). batch_in_flight: bool, curve_request: ?Pipe.RangeRequest(.acts), loss_request: ?Pipe.RangeRequest(.loss), steps_per_batch: u32, /// The GPU's training state on its way back to the CPU (`takeTheCpu`). state_request: ?Network.StateRequest, /// A batch's inputs: the grid's x values, as the job makes them (`sketch.sampleX`). sample_inputs: [sketch.sample_count]f32, }; fn initState(gpa: Allocator, f: *z.Frame, s: *State) !void { const font: z.Font = try z.loadFont(f, gpa, atkinson_mono_ttf, 20); const training_state: []f32 = try gpa.alloc(f32, kernels.most_state_floats); const payload_buffer: []u8 = try gpa.alloc(u8, kernels.registry.max_input); const result_buffer: []u8 = try gpa.alloc(u8, kernels.registry.max_output); var sample_inputs: [sketch.sample_count]f32 = undefined; var sample_xs: [sketch.sample_count]f64 = undefined; for (&sample_inputs, &sample_xs, 0..) |*sample_input, *sample_x, sample_index| { sample_input.* = sketch.sampleX(sample_index); sample_x.* = sample_input.*; } // The GPU's pipe, its pipelines made in the background: the CPU trains at once, and the GPU is offered once they // are all made (`drawMachine`). const gpu_pipe: ?Pipe = Pipe.initGpuInBackground(gpa, f.gpu.device, f.gpu.queue, &gpu_kernels) catch |err| none: { std.log.warn("zimrnum_fit: no pipe on the GPU ({s}): the CPU trains alone", .{@errorName(err)}); break :none null; }; const largest_target: f64 = sketch.largest_target; const settings: Settings = .{}; s.* = .{ .gpa = gpa, .font = font, .ui_host = z.UiHost.init(gpa, font), .drawing = .sine(), .settings = settings, .rate_exponent = log10(settings.rate), .fresh_start_due = false, .moments_reset_due = false, .runs_inline = false, .paused = false, .training_state = training_state, .parameter_count = 0, .steps_taken = 0, .steps_since_reset = 0, .curve = @splat(0), .loss = 0, .job = .{}, .payload_buffer = payload_buffer, .result_buffer = result_buffer, .steps_per_job = 1, .steps_in_flight = 0, .submitted_at_ms = 0, .last_job_steps = 0, .last_job_seconds = 0, .speed_window_start = 0, .speed_window_steps = 0, .steps_per_second = 0, .worst_frame_gap_ms = 0, .average_frame_ms = 0, .failure_name = @splat(0), .failure_length = 0, .shape_notice = @splat(0), .shape_notice_length = 0, .plot_state = .{ .x = .{ .min = -1.0, .max = 1.0 }, .y = .{ .min = -largest_target, .max = largest_target }, .fitted = true, }, .sample_xs = sample_xs, .drawing_ys = @splat(0), .network_ys = @splat(0), .stroke_last = .{ 0, 0 }, .started_at_ms = z.wgpu.nowMs(), .loss_seconds = @splat(0), .loss_values = @splat(0), .loss_count = 0, .loss_stride = 1, .landings_since_loss_point = 0, .loss_plot_state = .{}, .machine = .cpu, .wanted_machine = .cpu, .gpu_pipe = gpu_pipe, .gpu_network = null, .batch_in_flight = false, .curve_request = null, .loss_request = null, .steps_per_batch = 1, .state_request = null, .sample_inputs = sample_inputs, }; } fn deinit(gpa: Allocator, s: *State) void { // Cancels the job if it is still in flight: a thread's is reclaimed once it lands. s.job.deinit(); // The GPU's readbacks given up - their buffers wait for the device - then its network and its pipe. if (s.curve_request) |*request| { request.discard(); } if (s.loss_request) |*request| { request.discard(); } if (s.state_request) |*request| { request.discard(); } if (s.gpu_network) |network| { network.deinit(); } if (s.gpu_pipe) |*pipe| { pipe.deinit(); } gpa.free(s.training_state); gpa.free(s.payload_buffer); gpa.free(s.result_buffer); s.ui_host.deinit(); z.unloadFont(gpa, s.font); } /// A name kept in a fixed buffer, cut to its room: returns its length. fn keepName(destination: []u8, name: []const u8) usize { const kept_length: usize = @min(name.len, destination.len); @memcpy(destination[0..kept_length], name[0..kept_length]); return kept_length; } fn recordFailure(s: *State, failure_name: []const u8) void { s.failure_length = keepName(&s.failure_name, failure_name); std.log.err("zimrnum_fit: the training job failed: {s}", .{failure_name}); } /// The header of a job of `step_count` steps of the network `settings` describes. fn trainHeader( settings: Settings, step_count: u32, starts_fresh: bool, steps_taken: u32, ) kernels.TrainHeader { const header: kernels.TrainHeader = .{ .step_count = step_count, .hidden_layer_count = settings.hidden_layer_count, .hidden_width = settings.hidden_width, .activation = settings.activation, .optimizer = settings.optimizer, .rate = settings.rate, .momentum = settings.momentum, .starts_fresh = starts_fresh, .seed = settings.seed, .steps_taken = steps_taken, }; return header; } /// STEPS PER JOB, steered so that a job lasts about two frames. The kernel has no clock, so a job is timed from its /// submit to its landing: doubled when one lands within a frame, halved past four. fn steerStepsPerJob(s: *State) void { const landed_soon: bool = s.last_job_seconds < 0.5 * job_target_seconds; const landed_late: bool = s.last_job_seconds > 2.0 * job_target_seconds; if (landed_soon) { s.steps_per_job = @min(s.steps_per_job * 2, most_steps_per_job); } else if (landed_late) { s.steps_per_job = @max(s.steps_per_job / 2, 1); } } /// The seconds since the job in flight was submitted. fn secondsSinceSubmit(s: *const State) f32 { const elapsed_ms: f64 = z.wgpu.nowMs() - s.submitted_at_ms; return @floatCast(elapsed_ms / 1000.0); } /// One point of the loss chart, for the job just landed: every `loss_stride`-th landing is kept. When the room is /// full, every other point goes and the stride doubles - the whole run stays in view, in a room that never grows. fn recordLoss(s: *State) void { s.landings_since_loss_point += 1; if (s.landings_since_loss_point < s.loss_stride) { return; } s.landings_since_loss_point = 0; const room_is_full: bool = s.loss_count == loss_room; if (room_is_full) { for (0..loss_room / 2) |kept_index| { s.loss_seconds[kept_index] = s.loss_seconds[2 * kept_index + 1]; s.loss_values[kept_index] = s.loss_values[2 * kept_index + 1]; } s.loss_count = loss_room / 2; s.loss_stride *= 2; } const elapsed_ms: f64 = z.wgpu.nowMs() - s.started_at_ms; const loss: f64 = s.loss; s.loss_seconds[s.loss_count] = elapsed_ms / 1000.0; s.loss_values[s.loss_count] = @max(loss, smallest_loss_shown); s.loss_count += 1; } /// A landed result into the page's state: its head, the training's state, the curve. fn takeResult(s: *State, bytes: []const u8, job_seconds: f32) void { const head_bytes: usize = @sizeOf(kernels.TrainResultHead); if (bytes.len < head_bytes) { recordFailure(s, "ResultTooShort"); return; } var head: kernels.TrainResultHead = undefined; @memcpy(asBytes(&head), bytes[0..head_bytes]); const state_floats: usize = 3 * @as(usize, head.parameter_count); const result_is_whole: bool = state_floats <= s.training_state.len and bytes.len == head_bytes + kernels.resultFloatCount(head.parameter_count) * @sizeOf(f32); if (!result_is_whole) { recordFailure(s, "ResultDoesNotFit"); return; } const numbers: []const u8 = bytes[head_bytes..]; const state_bytes: usize = state_floats * @sizeOf(f32); @memcpy(sliceAsBytes(s.training_state[0..state_floats]), numbers[0..state_bytes]); @memcpy(sliceAsBytes(&s.curve), numbers[state_bytes..]); s.parameter_count = head.parameter_count; s.steps_taken = head.steps_taken; s.steps_since_reset += s.steps_in_flight; s.loss = head.loss; s.last_job_steps = s.steps_in_flight; s.last_job_seconds = job_seconds; s.speed_window_steps += s.steps_in_flight; steerStepsPerJob(s); recordLoss(s); } /// Takes the job's result once it has landed - a non-blocking poll, every frame, the same whether a worker, a thread /// or the inline fallback ran it - and releases the job, landed or failed, so that the next can be submitted. fn collectJob(s: *State) void { const landed_bytes: ?[]const u8 = s.job.pollInto(s.result_buffer) catch |err| { const job_name: []const u8 = s.job.errorName(); recordFailure(s, if (job_name.len > 0) job_name else @errorName(err)); s.job.deinit(); return; }; const bytes: []const u8 = landed_bytes orelse return; takeResult(s, bytes, secondsSinceSubmit(s)); s.job.deinit(); } /// THE SAME JOB ON THE FRAME's THREAD: the kernel called as a plain function, as `jobs` itself does where no worker /// can be had, into the page's own result buffer. The frame waits for every step of it. fn runJobHere(s: *State, header: kernels.TrainHeader, payload: []const u8) void { var job_arena: ArenaAllocator = .init(s.gpa); defer job_arena.deinit(); var result_writer: Writer = .fixed(s.result_buffer); kernels.trainSteps(job_arena.allocator(), header, payload, &result_writer) catch |err| { recordFailure(s, @errorName(err)); return; }; takeResult(s, result_writer.buffered(), secondsSinceSubmit(s)); } /// Submits the next job - unless one is in flight, one has failed, the training is paused or the machines are being /// switched - with the training's state, unless it starts fresh, and the drawing AS IT IS NOW: a change to the drawing /// reaches the training within a job. The panel's changes are made here, to the state the last job sent back. fn submitJob(s: *State) void { const has_failed: bool = s.failure_length > 0; const switch_is_pending: bool = s.wanted_machine != s.machine; if (s.job.inFlight() or has_failed or s.paused or switch_is_pending) { return; } const starts_fresh: bool = s.parameter_count == 0 or s.fresh_start_due; const parameter_count: usize = s.parameter_count; const resets_moments: bool = !starts_fresh and s.moments_reset_due; if (resets_moments) { @memset(s.training_state[parameter_count .. 3 * parameter_count], 0.0); s.steps_taken = 0; } if (starts_fresh) { s.steps_since_reset = 0; } s.fresh_start_due = false; s.moments_reset_due = false; const state_floats: usize = if (starts_fresh) 0 else 3 * parameter_count; const state_bytes: usize = state_floats * @sizeOf(f32); const target_bytes: usize = sketch.sample_count * @sizeOf(f32); @memcpy(s.payload_buffer[0..state_bytes], sliceAsBytes(s.training_state[0..state_floats])); @memcpy(s.payload_buffer[state_bytes..][0..target_bytes], sliceAsBytes(&s.drawing.targets)); const steps_taken: u32 = if (starts_fresh) 0 else s.steps_taken; const header: kernels.TrainHeader = trainHeader(s.settings, s.steps_per_job, starts_fresh, steps_taken); const payload: []const u8 = s.payload_buffer[0 .. state_bytes + target_bytes]; s.steps_in_flight = s.steps_per_job; s.submitted_at_ms = z.wgpu.nowMs(); if (s.runs_inline) { runJobHere(s, header, payload); return; } s.job = kernels.registry.submit(s.gpa, kernels.trainSteps, header, payload) catch |err| submit_failed: { recordFailure(s, @errorName(err)); break :submit_failed .{}; }; } /// How far the GPU's pipelines have come - null where there is no pipe on the GPU. Asked every frame: a pipe whose /// pipelines are made in the background may dispatch only once they all are (`pipelineProgress`). fn gpuProgress(s: *State) ?Pipe.PipelineProgress { if (s.gpu_pipe) |*pipe| { return pipe.pipelineProgress(); } return null; } /// THE GPU's NETWORK, made afresh from the seed for the panel's settings - the one before, if any, released. The very /// network a job builds (`kernels.networkSpec`), on the device's buffers instead of the twin's. fn makeGpuNetwork(s: *State) !*Network { if (s.gpu_network) |old_network| { old_network.deinit(); s.gpu_network = null; } var hidden_widths: [kernels.most_hidden_layers]u32 = undefined; const spec: kit_mlp.Spec = kernels.networkSpec(trainHeader(s.settings, 1, true, 0), &hidden_widths); const network: *Network = try Network.init(s.gpa, &s.gpu_pipe.?, spec); s.gpu_network = network; return network; } /// THE PANEL's CHANGES ON THE GPU, made before a batch as the CPU's are before a job (`submitJob`): a fresh start makes /// a new network; a new optimiser zeroes both moments and the step count; the rate and SGD's momentum are the /// network's spec, which each step reads as it is recorded (`KitMlp.recordOptimizerStep`). fn applySettingsOnTheGpu(s: *State) !*Network { const starts_fresh: bool = s.gpu_network == null or s.fresh_start_due; s.fresh_start_due = false; if (starts_fresh) { s.moments_reset_due = false; s.steps_since_reset = 0; return makeGpuNetwork(s); } const network: *Network = s.gpu_network.?; if (s.moments_reset_due) { s.moments_reset_due = false; const zeros: []f32 = try s.gpa.alloc(f32, network.param_count); defer s.gpa.free(zeros); @memset(zeros, 0.0); network.pipe.upload(.adam_m, zeros); network.pipe.upload(.adam_v, zeros); network.adam_step = 0; } var hidden_widths: [kernels.most_hidden_layers]u32 = undefined; const wanted: kit_mlp.Spec = kernels.networkSpec(trainHeader(s.settings, 1, false, 0), &hidden_widths); network.spec.rate = wanted.rate; network.spec.optimizer = wanted.optimizer; return network; } /// The most steps one recording holds for the panel's network, so that a batch stays one submission: a step /// dispatches every layer forward, the loss and its gradient, up to three kernels a layer backward, and the optimiser /// (`KitMlp.recordStep`). fn mostStepsPerBatch(settings: Settings) u32 { const layer_count: u32 = settings.hidden_layer_count + 1; const dispatches_per_step: u32 = 4 * layer_count + 3; return @max(Pipe.recording_slots / dispatches_per_step, 1); } /// STEPS PER BATCH, steered like a job's but on the frames too: doubled while a batch comes back within two frames and /// the frames keep time, halved when one takes past four or the frames run late - a GPU kept too busy holds the /// page's own drawing back. fn steerStepsPerBatch(s: *State) void { const frames_are_late: bool = s.average_frame_ms > late_frame_ms; const came_back_late: bool = s.last_job_seconds > longest_batch_seconds; const came_back_soon: bool = s.last_job_seconds <= job_target_seconds; if (frames_are_late or came_back_late) { s.steps_per_batch = @max(s.steps_per_batch / 2, 1); } else if (came_back_soon) { s.steps_per_batch = @min(s.steps_per_batch * 2, mostStepsPerBatch(s.settings)); } } /// THE NEXT BATCH ON THE GPU - unless one is in flight, one has failed, the training is paused or the machines are /// being switched: the drawing as it is now, `steps_per_batch` steps recorded as one submission, then the curve and the /// loss asked back. The frame never waits for them (`collectBatch`). fn submitBatch(s: *State) void { const has_failed: bool = s.failure_length > 0; const switch_is_pending: bool = s.wanted_machine != s.machine; if (s.batch_in_flight or has_failed or s.paused or switch_is_pending) { return; } const network: *Network = applySettingsOnTheGpu(s) catch |err| { recordFailure(s, @errorName(err)); return; }; network.setBatch(&s.sample_inputs, &s.drawing.targets); network.trainSteps(s.steps_per_batch); s.curve_request = network.requestOutputs(s.gpa) catch |err| { recordFailure(s, @errorName(err)); return; }; s.loss_request = network.pipe.requestRange(s.gpa, .loss, 0, 1) catch |err| { recordFailure(s, @errorName(err)); return; }; s.batch_in_flight = true; s.steps_in_flight = s.steps_per_batch; s.submitted_at_ms = z.wgpu.nowMs(); } /// Takes the GPU's batch once both its readbacks have landed - polled every frame, each landing as it arrives. fn collectBatch(s: *State) void { if (!s.batch_in_flight) { return; } if (s.curve_request) |*request| { if (request.collect(&s.curve)) { s.curve_request = null; } } if (s.loss_request) |*request| { var loss: [1]f32 = undefined; if (request.collect(&loss)) { s.loss = loss[0]; s.loss_request = null; } } const batch_has_landed: bool = s.curve_request == null and s.loss_request == null; if (!batch_has_landed) { return; } s.batch_in_flight = false; const network: *Network = s.gpu_network.?; Its jobs work in the kit's CPU-twin buffers - the kernel module's globals - and the page LENDS /// them: its frame never dispatches on a CPU pipe of the kit while a job runs, and its GPU pipe writes only the /// device's buffers. (build.zig's `JobKernelModules`): the job as a worker runs it - the kit's CPU twin, with no host. //! //! Each check compares runs made one after the other on the twin, whose buffers are ONE set, shared by every CPU pipe //! of the module (claude.md, "TWO CPU PIPES OF ONE MODULE ARE ONE SET OF BUFFERS"). So every buffer is poisoned with //! NaN before each run - a run reading anything it neither wrote nor was given shows it - and what is compared are //! the bytes each run sent back, copies, never the buffers. const std = @import("std"); /// Adam over tanh, SGD with momentum over relu: each of the header's two choices both ways. const cases = [_]Case{ .{ .activation = .tanh, .optimizer = .adam, .kit_activation = .tanh, .kit_optimizer = .adam }, .{ .activation = .relu, .optimizer = .sgd, .kit_activation = .relu, .kit_optimizer = .{ .sgd = .{ .momentum = momentum } }, }, }; /// A job header for `steps` steps of a case's network. fn caseHeader( check_case: Case, steps: u32, starts_fresh: bool, steps_taken: u32, ) kernels.TrainHeader { const train_header: kernels.TrainHeader = .{ .step_count = steps, .hidden_layer_count = hidden_widths.len, .hidden_width = hidden_widths[0], .activation = check_case.activation, .optimizer = check_case.optimizer, .rate = rate, .momentum = momentum, .starts_fresh = starts_fresh, .seed = seed, .steps_taken = steps_taken, }; return train_header; } /// NaN over every buffer of the kit's CPU twin that a job reads or writes. fn poisonTheTwin(pipe: *Pipe, poison: []const f32) void { pipe.upload(.acts, poison[0..zn_mlp.acts_len]); Returns a copy of /// what it wrote, owned by the caller. fn runJob(gpa: Allocator, train_header: kernels.TrainHeader, payload: []const u8) ![]u8 { var job_arena: ArenaAllocator = .init(gpa); defer job_arena.deinit(); const room: []u8 = try job_arena.allocator().alloc(u8, result_room); var result_writer: Writer = .fixed(room); try kernels.trainSteps(job_arena.allocator(), train_header, payload, &result_writer); return gpa.dupe(u8, result_writer.buffered()); } /// A result's head. fn resultHead(result: []const u8) kernels.TrainResultHead { var head: kernels.TrainResultHead = undefined; @memcpy(asBytes(&head), result[0..@sizeOf(kernels.TrainResultHead)]); return head; } /// A result's training state - the weights and both moments - as bytes. fn stateBytes(result: []const u8) []const u8 { const head: kernels.TrainResultHead = resultHead(result); const state_byte_count: usize = 3 * @as(usize, head.parameter_count) * @sizeOf(f32); return result[@sizeOf(kernels.TrainResultHead)..][0..state_byte_count]; } /// A job's payload as the page builds it (`submitJob`): the state the last job sent back, unless there is none and /// the job starts fresh, then the targets. fn payloadFrom(gpa: Allocator, last_result: ?[]const u8, targets: []const f32) ![]u8 { const state_bytes: []const u8 = if (last_result) |result| stateBytes(result) else &.{}; const target_bytes: []const u8 = sliceAsBytes(targets); const payload: []u8 = try gpa.alloc(u8, state_bytes.len + target_bytes.len); @memcpy(payload[0..state_bytes.len], state_bytes); @memcpy(payload[state_bytes.len..], target_bytes); return payload; } test "zimrnum_fit's job: its steps are KitMlp's own on the twin, bit for bit" { // The job, fresh, takes `step_count` steps; then KitMlp, from a `Spec` written out by hand, takes as many on the // same grid and targets. const poison: []f32 = try gpa.alloc(f32, poison_length); defer gpa.free(poison); @memset(poison, nan(f32)); const targets: [sketch.sample_count]f32 = sketch.Sketch.sine().targets; var inputs: [sketch.sample_count]f32 = undefined; for (&inputs, 0..) |*input, sample_index| { input.* = sketch.sampleX(sample_index); } for (cases) |check_case| { poisonTheTwin(&pipe, poison); const payload: []u8 = try payloadFrom(gpa, null, &targets); defer direct_arena.deinit(); const arena: Allocator = direct_arena.allocator(); const spec: kit_mlp.Spec = .{ .inputs = 1, .hidden = &hidden_widths, .outputs = 1, .act = check_case.kit_activation, .rows = sketch.sample_count, .optimizer = check_case.kit_optimizer, .rate = rate, .seed = seed, }; const network: *Network = try Network.init(arena, &pipe, spec); network.setBatch(&inputs, &targets); network.trainSteps(step_count); const parameter_count: usize = network.param_count; const direct_floats: []f32 = try arena.alloc(f32, kernels.resultFloatCount(parameter_count)); var state: kit_mlp.TrainingState = .{ .weights = direct_floats[0..parameter_count], .first_moments = direct_floats[parameter_count..][0..parameter_count], .second_moments = direct_floats[2 * parameter_count ..][0..parameter_count], .step_count = 0, }; var state_request: Network.StateRequest = try network.requestState(arena); try expect(state_request.collect(&state)); var curve_request: Pipe.RangeRequest(.acts) = try network.requestOutputs(arena); try expect(curve_request.collect(direct_floats[3 * parameter_count ..][0..sketch.sample_count])); const loss: []const f32 = pipe.readLatest(.loss) orelse return error.NoLoss; const job_head: kernels.TrainResultHead = resultHead(job_result); try expectEqual(state.step_count, job_head.steps_taken); try expectEqual(parameter_count, job_head.parameter_count); try expectEqual(@as(u32, @bitCast(loss[0])), @as(u32, @bitCast(job_head.loss))); const job_floats: []const u8 = job_result[@sizeOf(kernels.TrainResultHead)..]; try expectEqualSlices(u8, sliceAsBytes(direct_floats), job_floats); } } test "zimrnum_fit's job: one job of K steps is K jobs of one, the state carried in the bytes" { // As the page chains them: each job of one step is given the state the last one sent back and the steps it has // taken (Adam's bias corrections read them). Had any of the training lived outside those bytes - a moment, the // step count - or had a job read anything it was not given, the chain would part from the one long job. const gpa: Allocator = testing_allocator; var pipe: Pipe = .initCpu(); const poison: []f32 = try gpa.alloc(f32, poison_length); defer gpa.free(poison); @memset(poison, nan(f32)); const targets: [sketch.sample_count]f32 = sketch.Sketch.sine().targets; const fresh_payload: []u8 = try payloadFrom(gpa, null, &targets); defer gpa.free(fresh_payload); for (cases) |check_case| { poisonTheTwin(&pipe, poison); const long_job: []u8 = try runJob(gpa, caseHeader(check_case, step_count, true, 0), fresh_payload); defer gpa.free(long_job); poisonTheTwin(&pipe, poison); var chained: []u8 = try runJob(gpa, caseHeader(check_case, 1, true, 0), fresh_payload); defer gpa.free(chained); for (1..step_count) |_| { poisonTheTwin(&pipe, poison); const payload: []u8 = try payloadFrom(gpa, chained, &targets); defer gpa.free(payload); const steps_taken: u32 = resultHead(chained).steps_taken; const next: []u8 = try runJob(gpa, caseHeader(check_case, 1, false, steps_taken), payload); gpa.free(chained); chained = next; } try expectEqual(step_count, resultHead(chained).steps_taken); try expectEqualSlices(u8, long_job, chained); } }

//! examples/zimrnum_fit/sketch.zig - THE DRAWING: a curve you reshape with the pointer, kept as one target y for each //! of `sample_count` x values evenly over [-1, 1] (`src/notes/zimrnum_fit_plan.md`, D5). Every sample always has a //! target, so the network trains on the whole grid every step (D6), and its outputs over the grid ARE the curve drawn. //! //! Pure - no engine, no allocator: the page draws it and the job builds its inputs from the same grid (`sampleX`), so //! the two can never disagree on where a sample sits. const zm = @import("zm"); const clamp = zm.clamp; const float = zm.float; const lerp = zm.lerp; const roundi = zm.roundi; const sinTurns = zm.sinTurns; const Vec2 = zm.Vec2; /// Samples of the curve - and so rows of the training batch, every step. pub const sample_count: u32 = 512; /// How far a target may go from zero: the plot's top and bottom. pub const largest_target: f32 = 1.5; /// Where sample `sample_index` sits: evenly over [-1, 1], both ends included. pub fn sampleX(sample_index: usize) f32 { const last_index: f32 = float(sample_count - 1); return -1.0 + 2.0 * float(sample_index) / last_index; } /// The sample nearest `x`, clamped to the grid. fn nearestSample(x: f32) usize { const last_index: f32 = float(sample_count - 1); const position: f32 = clamp((x + 1.0) * 0.5 * last_index, 0.0, last_index); return roundi(usize, position); } pub const Sketch = struct { /// The target y of each sample. targets: [sample_count]f32, /// Moves on with every change, so that whoever shipped the targets can tell they are no longer what it shipped. version: u32, /// The curve the page starts with: two periods of a sine. pub fn sine() Sketch { var sketch: Sketch = .{ .targets = undefined, .version = 0 }; sketch.drawSine(); return sketch; } pub fn drawSine(sketch: *Sketch) void { for (&sketch.targets, 0..) |*target, sample_index| { target.* = 0.8 * sinTurns(sampleX(sample_index)); } sketch.version +%= 1; } pub fn clear(sketch: *Sketch) void { @memset(&sketch.targets, 0.0); sketch.version +%= 1; } /// PAINT one segment of a stroke, from where the pointer was to where it is, in the plot's units: every sample /// between the two x takes the straight line's y there - so a fast stroke, its frames far apart, leaves no gap. pub fn paintSegment(sketch: *Sketch, from: Vec2, to: Vec2) void { const first_index: usize = nearestSample(@min(from[0], to[0])); const last_index: usize = nearestSample(@max(from[0], to[0])); const span: f32 = to[0] - from[0]; const is_vertical: bool = @abs(span) < 1.0e-6; for (first_index..last_index + 1) |sample_index| { const along: f32 = if (is_vertical) 1.0 else clamp((sampleX(sample_index) - from[0]) / span, 0.0, 1.0); const height: f32 = lerp(from[1], to[1], along); sketch.targets[sample_index] = clamp(height, -largest_target, largest_target); } sketch.version +%= 1; } };
